title: The Winter of Vessel Farm
premise: In 1974, folklorist Ivo Whitlock arrives in the snowbound village of Hollowmere to record its songs, only to find that every ballad ends at the same missing verse. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath Vessel Farm, the village's oldest families begin dying in ways that mirror the verses, and Ivo discovers his own arrival was foretold in the song: he is the 'listener' the thing below has been waiting for. As the well refills and the winter deepens, Ivo must choose between fleeing with what he knows or staying until sunrise to speak the forbidden verse aloud, breaking the bargain the founders made generations ago. He survives the night by giving up the truth he came for — burning his recordings and singing the verse himself — sealing the door forever but leaving him the last keeper of a story no one will ever believe.
about_author: T. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing field recordings of disappearing regional music across northern England. They write horror about the places where folklore refuses to stay dead.

chapters.title: The Bus Stops Short of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Ivo Whitlock's POV. Arriving in deep snow, Ivo finds the driver will go no further than the farm road, muttering about 'the listening season.' The village appears on no recent map. Emotional beat: quiet unease dressed as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the Lamb and Lantern inn, landlady Edith Marrow agrees to one recording of each ballad, then goes pale when Ivo asks her to repeat 'The Well-Wife's Lament.' Every villager refuses. Beat: first crack in his skepticism.

chapters.title: The Missing Verse
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Reviewing tapes at night, Ivo discovers every version of every song skips the same stanza — a silence where words should be. He transcribes the gap as blank lines. Beat: scholarly obsession taking root.

chapters.title: Vessel Farm
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo visits the derelict Vessel Farm to interview old Tam Vessel, the last of his line, who lives without electricity and salt-lines every doorway. Tam warns him: 'They didn't seal it to keep something out.' Beat: dread disguised as eccentricity.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Danny Oakes' POV. A government survey team arrives to dig test pits near the old wellhead despite village objections. Danny notices the villagers counting them — nine strangers, nine shovels. Beat: intrusion into a place that was waiting.

chapters.title: The Door, Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Forty feet down, the crew strikes a stone door whose bolts are thrown from within. Behind it, something knocks back. Beat: wonder curdling into terror; the impossible made physical.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Summoned as the nearest 'educated man,' Ivo examines the door and recognizes carvings matching the ballads' marginalia. Tam Vessel arrives and says the founders built the door around something they welcomed. Beat: belief begins against his will.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. The landlady tells Ivo the village pays a tithe each generation: names given freely at the well so the thing below stays fed and stays down. Her own sister's name is on the oldest list. Beat: guilt and complicity revealed.

chapters.title: First Death
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. A crewman who pocketed a carved bolt is found frozen upright in a warm room, mouth full of well-water. The coroner writes 'exposure.' Beat: the rules are real, and breaking them kills.

chapters.title: The Song Begins Again
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. That night every radio in Hollowmere plays static shaped like the Lament — including the missing verse, half-audible. Ivo records it; the tape plays back blank. Beat: the supernatural closes in on his instruments and his certainty.

chapters.title: Nine Names
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. The parish register shows the excavation crew numbered exactly nine — the tithe count. Edith realizes the digging wasn't coincidence; someone above invited them. Beat: paranoia turns inward toward the village itself.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The old man reveals the Vessels have been door-keepers for two centuries, feeding it names so it never learns to open the door itself. His line is ending; he needs a successor who can hear the verse. Beat: desperate inheritance, reluctant recruitment.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. The excavated well shaft, pumped dry for days, fills overnight with water warm as breath. Down in the floodlight, shapes move beneath the surface like reflections with no source. Beat: rising dread; the deadline becomes visible.

chapters.title: Ivo Refuses
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Offered the keeper's role, Ivo packs to leave, recordings under his arm. The bus never comes; the road behind him ends in unbroken snow where tire tracks should be. Beat: denial shattered; escape is not among the options.

chapters.title: Second Death
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. The vicar, who burned the parish's tithe lists years ago hoping to end the pact, drowns in his locked vestry. In his hand: a page torn from the register bearing Ivo's name, ink still wet. Beat: betrayal by the village's own history.

chapters.title: My Name Is Already Written
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Confronting Edith, Ivo learns his invitation letter — which he believed came from a university colleague — bears the parish seal. He was chosen before he ever chose to come. Beat: the horror of predestination; loyalty to truth vs. self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Undercroft
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam leads Ivo beneath the farmhouse to the original keepers' chamber: wax cylinders, ledgers of names, and a wall of scratched tally-marks counting winters survived. Beat: awe and grief; the scale of the long obedience.

chapters.title: What the Verse Says
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cross-referencing fragments, Ivo reconstructs the missing stanza: it isn't a warding charm but a promise — the founders swore to keep listening forever, and the thing below keeps its side by keeping everything else out. Beat: revelation reframes everything; survival has always had a price.

chapters.title: Danny Breaks
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Haunted by his drowned crewman, Danny tries to dynamite the door. The charge fails to detonate; instead every window in the village frosts over from the inside. Beat: power corrupts — force meets ancient patience and loses.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. In the Lamb and Lantern, the surviving families vote: give the stranger to the well and end the tithe forever. Only Edith and Tam object. Beat: loyalty vs. truth — the community chooses survival over honesty.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Snow
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Warned by Edith, Ivo flees across the fields toward the ridge road, pursued by neighbors carrying lanterns and hymnals. The snow erases his tracks ahead of him, herding him back toward the farm. Beat: terror and heartbreak; the hunted cannot leave.

chapters.title: Tam Stands in the Doorway
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam blocks the mob at his gate, invoking the old law: the listener belongs to the door, not the village. They retreat — but not far. Beat: sacrifice and defiance; an old man spends his last authority.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Winter solstice. Tam explains: tonight the well refills completely, and if no keeper sings the verse at sunrise, the door opens from both sides. Beat: the stakes crystallize into a single deadline.

chapters.title: Edith's Choice
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith burns the tithe ledger publicly, freeing the village's dead names — and damning them all to the thing's attention. She does it so Ivo won't be bound by other people's bargains. Beat: costly loyalty; truth set free at terrible price.

chapters.title: The Water Rises
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. The well floods the undercroft; the mob, scattered by frost and fear, takes shelter in the church. Danny, half-mad, starts reciting the verse from memory — wrong, and the water rises faster. Beat: chaos; good intentions weaponized badly.

chapters.title: Voices in the Tapes
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Playing his recordings one last time, Ivo hears the drowned crewman's voice layered under the ballads, teaching him the true cadence of the verse. The dead are keeping their side of the promise. Beat: eerie grace; help from beyond the threshold.

chapters.title: Tam Goes Down
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Too frail to reach the door chamber before dawn, Tam gives Ivo the keeper's iron key and his family's confession to carry. 'Sing it true,' he says, and walks into the flood to buy time. Beat: devastating sacrifice; the torch passed mid-crisis.

chapters.title: The Mob at the Farm
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The villagers, led by Danny, surround Vessel Farm demanding Ivo be given to the well as the 'clean' solution. Edith stands with him. Beat: siege; loyalty tested at gunpoint of pitchforks and panic.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Descending the flooded stair as the water climbs, Ivo reaches the door and sees through its hairline seam: not darkness but a vast patient attention, older than the village, lonely as winter. Beat: confrontation with the sublime; fear becomes pity.

chapters.title: The False Sunrise
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Dawn comes gray and wrong — the sun rises in the west. The village realizes the solstice hasn't ended; time itself is held. Beat: cosmic escalation; the deadline stretches into nightmare.

chapters.title: Danny's Redemption
chapters.summary: Danny's POV. Understanding at last that the verse must be sung true, not forced, Danny holds the mob back from killing Ivo, turning his authority against the crowd he led. Beat: redemption arc completes; power finally serves truth.

chapters.title: The Verse Spoken
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the door, Ivo sings the missing stanza — not as a ward but as a promise kept: we remember you, we name you, you are not forgotten. The knocking stops. The water stills. Beat: climax; the monster is answered with witness, not violence.

chapters.title: Sunrise, For Real
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The sun rises east. The door's bolts slide home on their own — sealed from the inside once more, but now by consent rather than captivity. Ivo climbs out into ordinary cold. Beat: release; exhaustion and fragile triumph.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Tam is gone; three villagers died in the flood; the tithe is broken, meaning the village must now simply trust. Edith buries the ledger ashes under the wellhead. Beat: mourning; survival's bill comes due in grief.

chapters.title: What Ivo Keeps
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Packing his tapes, Ivo finds them all blank except one: Tam's voice, singing the complete Lament, preserved like a gift. He understands he is now the only archive. Beat: bittersweet inheritance; the folklorist becomes the folklore.

chapters.title: The Village Lets Him Go
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The bus, impossibly, waits at the crossroads. Villagers watch from doorways — some grateful, some hollow-eyed with shame. No one says goodbye. Beat: exile and mercy intertwined.

chapters.title: The Road Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the journey south, Ivo passes the ridge and looks back: Hollowmere is simply gone from the landscape, a valley of untouched snow. Beat: uncanny closure; the price of survival is being erased from the world you saved.

chapters.title: The Blank Chapter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, framed as journal entries. Back in London, Ivo tries to write his report and finds himself writing the same blank stanza he once transcribed. His pen stops at the gap every time. Beat: haunting aftermath; some truths resist being told.

chapters.title: The Listener's Duty
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Years later, Ivo receives a letter postmarked Hollowmere, containing a single pressed snowdrop and a request: another listener is needed. He books the train. Beat: acceptance of the cycle; loyalty chosen freely this time.

chapters.title: Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing frame. On the bus short of Hollowmere, Ivo teaches the driver the Lament — all of it, including the verse — and makes him sing it twice. The snow eases. Beat: resolution; the curse of silence broken by a story finally told whole.
